Description: Legal system based on Dharma (duties) and Neeti (ethics). Arthashastra by Kautilya discusses law and punishment.
Significance: Foundation of moral and ethical legal principles in India.

Description: Compilation of Islamic law under Emperor Aurangzeb, governing criminal justice and personal laws.
Significance: codified Islamic legal principles in India.

Description: Established the Supreme Court at Calcutta, marking the beginning of a formal British legal system in India.
Significance: Introduction of English common law elements in India.

Description: Established under Lord Macaulay to codify Indian laws.
Significance: Led to the drafting of the IPC.

Description: Comprehensive code covering substantive criminal law, drafted by Lord Macaulay. Came into force in 1862.
Significance: The backbone of Indian criminal law for over 160 years.

Description: Established the organized police force structure in India.
Significance: Created the modern police system.

Description: Codified the rules of evidence admissibility in Indian courts, drafted by Sir James Fitzjames Stephen.
Significance: Standardized evidentiary rules.

Description: First comprehensive code for criminal procedure, consolidating various acts.
Significance: Laid the procedural framework for criminal trials.

Description: Came into force on Jan 26, 1950. Established India as a Republic and guaranteed Fundamental Rights (Articles 14-32).
Significance: Supreme law of the land, source of all legal authority.

Description: Replaced the 1898 Code. Separated Judiciary from Executive. Introduced Anticipatory Bail (Section 438).
Significance: Modernized criminal procedure and enhanced judicial independence.

Event: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Description: Supreme Court expanded Article 21, creating the 'Due Process' doctrine. Procedure established by law must be fair, just, and reasonable.
Significance: Cornerstone of personal liberty jurisprudence.

Event: Moti Ram v. State of MP
Description: Justice Krishna Iyer declared 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception'. Criticized excessive surety demands.
Significance: Humanized bail jurisprudence.

Description: Criminalized cruelty by husband or relatives aginst a woman.
Significance: Addressed domestic violence and dowry deaths.

Description: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. Introduced strict liability and stringent bail conditions (Section 37).
Significance: War on drugs legislation with strict penal provisions.

Description: Supreme Court guidelines against sexual harassment at workplace.
Significance: Precursor to the POSH Act, 2013.

Description: Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Introduced strict twin conditions for bail (Section 45).
Significance: Addressed economic crimes and terrorist financing.

Description: Introduced Section 436A to release undertrials who have served half the maximum sentence.
Significance: Relief for poor undertrials ensuring right to speedy trial.

Description: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Gender-neutral law protecting children.
Significance: Special courts and child-friendly procedures.

Description: Expanded definition of rape, introduced new offences (stalking, voyeurism), and increased punishments.
Significance: Strengthened laws against sexual violence.

Event: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
Description: Supreme Court guidelines to check automatic arrests in cases with punishment up to 7 years. Mandated Section 41A Notice.
Significance: Prevented unnecessary arrests and harassment.

Event: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Description: Right to Privacy declared a fundamental right under Article 21.
Significance: Expanded the scope of personal liberty.

Event: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
Description: Decriminalized consensual homosexual acts (Section 377 IPC).
Significance: Victory for LGBTQ+ rights and personal autonomy.

Description: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) passed to replace IPC, CrPC, and Evidence Act.
Significance: Decolonization of Indian criminal justice system.

Description: BNS, BNSS, and BSA effectively replaced the colonial-era codes from July 1, 2024. Introduced e-FIR, community service, and terrorism definitions.
Significance: Major overhaul of the criminal justice administration.
